items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: When I was with Wickliffe's band here in 1920, Wickliffe's jazz band, I was playing violin, and Jimmy Paloa was playing plenty of sax.

ctx.x: I think by that time, Paloa, was that his name?

Yeah, Jimmy Paloa. I know he lived down the street from me. When I was with Wickliffe's band here in 1920, Wickliffe's jazz band, I was playing violin, and Jimmy Paloa was playing plenty of sax. And he was playing off cello parts, and then they had living. See, that's where they did the orchestration. That was before they started arranging for the three saxophones, two altos and a tenor. And so I got to, I had finished the harmony course, you call it musicology, before my money stopped coming in and I had to stop…
